# pycausalml {.pkg-name}

<p class="pkg-meta"><strong>Version:</strong> 0.2.0 · <strong>Requires:</strong> Python ≥ 3.9 · <strong>License:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/zia207/PyCausalML/blob/main/LICENSE">MIT</a></p>

Classical and deep causal inference in one installable package. Trees, uplift, meta-learners, double machine learning, treatment policies, Bayesian quasi-experiments, and the neural models from [PyDeepCausalML](https://github.com/zia207/PyDeepCausalML) share one import.

```{.bash copy="true"}
pip install https://github.com/zia207/PyCausalML/releases/download/v0.2.0/pycausalml-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

## What is it? {#what-is-it}

**PyCausalML** 0.2.0 extends [PyDeepCausalML 0.2.0](https://github.com/zia207/PyDeepCausalML/releases/tag/v0.2.0) and keeps every public estimator from that release (`TARNet`, `DragonNet`, `NOTEARS`, `TCDF`, and the rest). On top of those neural models it adds tree and forest estimators, uplift learners, meta-learners, double machine learning, treatment policies, and Bayesian quasi-experiments.

`import pycausalml` and `import pydeepcausalml` both work after installation. The deep-learning release on its own is still [PyDeepCausalML v0.2.0](https://github.com/zia207/PyDeepCausalML/releases/tag/v0.2.0).

Use it when you need to:

- Estimate **conditional average treatment effects** with honest trees, forests, meta-learners, or neural nets
- Score **uplift** on a binary outcome and choose **who should be treated**
- Estimate a constant effect with a **confidence interval** (double machine learning, neural DML)
- Run **quasi-experiments**: difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables
- Put **Bayesian uncertainty** on a causal network, a structural model, or a quasi-experiment
- Discover **causal graphs** from static or time-series data
- Train neural models on **CPU, CUDA, or Apple MPS** with the same scikit-learn style API

## Installation {#installation}

Requires Python ≥ 3.9. PyTorch ≥ 2.0 is included because the deep models are part of this distribution.

Install release [v0.2.0](https://github.com/zia207/PyCausalML/releases/tag/v0.2.0):

```bash
pip install https://github.com/zia207/PyCausalML/releases/download/v0.2.0/pycausalml-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

From source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zia207/PyCausalML.git
cd PyCausalML
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

Plotting (`matplotlib` / `seaborn`) and the optional libraries:

```bash
pip install -e ".[plot]"
pip install -e ".[dowhy,econml,causallearn,uber,doubleml,causalpy,skgrf,shap,boost]"
```

## Main features {#main-features}

| Module | What it estimates |
|---|---|
| `pycausalml.tree_based_models` | Honest trees, doubly robust forests, survival and instrumental forests, boosted causal models |
| `pycausalml.uplift_learners` | Uplift trees and forests, interaction trees, uplift XGBoost, Qini curves |
| `pycausalml.meta_learners` | S, T, X, R, and DR learners, plus domain adaptation |
| `pycausalml.double_machine_learning` | Partially linear, linear, sparse, nonparametric, kernel, and interactive DML |
| `pycausalml.policy_learners` | Doubly robust policy learner, policy tree, and policy forest |
| `pycausalml.bayesian_causalML` | Bayesian DiD, RDD, ITS, IV, synthetic control, causal networks, structural models |
| `pydeepcausalml` | TARNet, CFRNet, DragonNet, GANITE, CausalVAE, NOTEARS, TCDF, and the rest of the neural catalog |

Optional backends in `pycausalml.integrations` wrap DoWhy, EconML, causal-learn, Uber CausalML, DoubleML, CausalPy, and `skgrf` when those libraries are installed.

## Quickstart {#quickstart}

Classical estimators share `fit(X, treatment, y)` and return NumPy arrays of conditional average treatment effects.

```python
from pycausalml import DRLearner, PartiallyLinearDML, synthetic_data
from pycausalml.data import make_linear_treatment

data = synthetic_data(n=1000, p=6, sigma=0.8, mode=2, random_state=0)
dr = DRLearner(learner="gbr", n_estimators=40, random_state=0).fit(
    data["X"], data["w"], data["y"]
)
print("CATE:", dr.predict(data["X"][:5]))
print("ATE:", dr.average_treatment_effect())

linear = make_linear_treatment(n=800, tau=2.0, random_state=0)
dml = PartiallyLinearDML(model_y="ridge", random_state=0).fit(
    linear["X"], linear["w"], linear["y"]
)
print("DML effect:", dml.effect(), "95% CI:", dml.confidence_interval())
```

Neural estimators use the same top-level import:

```python
from pycausalml import DragonNet
from pydeepcausalml.datasets import make_confounded_data

df = make_confounded_data(n=2000, random_state=0)
X = df[["age", "education", "prior_income"]].values
est = DragonNet(epochs=50, random_state=0).fit(
    X, df["treatment"].values, df["outcome"].values
)
print("ATE:", est.predict_ate(X))
```

## Choosing an estimator {#choosing-an-estimator}

| Question | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Honest tree or forest CATE, with a doubly robust score | `CausalTree`, `CausalForest`, `DRLearner` |
| Uplift on a binary outcome | `UpliftRandomForest`, `UpliftXGBoost` |
| Constant effect with a confidence interval | `PartiallyLinearDML`, `NeuralDML` |
| Who should be treated? | `PolicyLearner`, `DRPolicyTree` |
| Threshold, before/after, or a single treated unit | `RegressionDiscontinuity`, `DifferenceInDifferences`, `SyntheticControl` |
| Bayesian uncertainty for a network or a quasi-experiment | `bayesian_causalML` |
| Neural effect on i.i.d. data | `TARNet`, `CFRNet`, `DragonNet` |
| Which variables cause which? | `NOTEARSLinear`, `DAGGNN`, `TCDF` |
